name: Tiglath-pileser
description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: Pul the king of Assyria comes against the land, and Menahem gives him a thousand talents of silver to confirm the kingdom in his hand.

note.label: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House

points: “And Pul the king of Assyria came against the land”, against Ephraim. Write this down: Pul is Tiglath-pileser the Third; Pul is short for his name. Pul was an Assyrian king.

“Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver, that his hand might be with him to confirm the kingdom in his hand.” Menahem paid the Assyrian king tax to make sure he stays ruler, stays reigning over the land.

note.label: Gentiles: What Happened to Northern Kingdom?

points: Came Tiglathpileser king of Assyria and carried them captive to Assyria. This is what we were reading about in the book of Amos earlier.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: “In the days of Pekah king of Israel came Tiglath–pileser king of Assyria”: the same Pul we read about earlier, same guy, the Third. He took Gilead, Galilee and “all the land of Naphtali, and carried them captive to Assyria.” This is the first wave. The first wave of the Northern Kingdom being deported out of the land and taken into Assyria was right here; it was done in waves. Pekah began to reign in the fifty-second year of Uzziah, and Pul conquered the Northern Kingdom at this time.

note.label: Gentiles: What Happened to Northern Kingdom?

points: God stirred up Pul, or Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, to carry away Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh. The northern kingdom was taken in waves, not all at once.
That's Pul. So, he went and conquered Ephraim. This green is all his provinces here. You see the arrows where he went.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

points: Because of this the Most High stirred up the spirit of Pul, that is Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, who carried Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh into captivity unto this day.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 5: The Tribes East of Jordan and Their Captivity
